sections.heading: C — Restrictions, implied consent, false identification and MVA administrative actions
sections.markdown:
## C — Restrictions, implied consent, false identification and MVA administrative actions

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A47
Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and the MVA may place restrictions on your license to keep your driving safe. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A47
A restriction limits your driving privileges and can come from your license type or from breaking motor vehicle laws; driving against a restriction is a serious offense that can cost you your privileges. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A47
Seat belt, passenger, nighttime and wireless device restrictions apply to graduated license holders under 18. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A47
A Provisional License holder must always wear a seat belt, and every passenger must use a seat belt or child safety seat. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A47
A provisional driver under 18 may not drive unsupervised with passengers under 18 for the first 151 days, unless the passengers are immediate family. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A47
During that period an unrelated passenger under 18 may ride along only when a qualified supervising driver is also in the vehicle. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A47
Immediate family for the passenger rule means a spouse, child, stepchild, sibling or stepsibling, or any relative living at your address. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A47
A Provisional License holder may drive unsupervised from 12:00 midnight to 5:00 a.m. only when going to, from or during a job. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A47
The other nighttime exceptions are trips to or from an organized volunteer program, an official school activity, or an athletic event or training session you take part in. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A47
Provisional License and Learner's Permit holders may not use any wireless communication device while driving, hands-free included, except to call 911 in an emergency. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A47
By driving or trying to drive on a road or on private property open to the public in Maryland, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test when an officer asks. [A47]
Why it matters: this is implied consent; the agreement comes with the act of driving.
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A47
If an officer has reason to think you are impaired by drugs, alcohol or a controlled substance, a drug recognition expert may ask you to submit to a blood test. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A47
Your license will be suspended if a test shows a blood alcohol concentration of .08 percent or more. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A48
Drug impairment counts too: having drugs in your system that impair you leads the MVA to suspend your license. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A48
Refusing a test also costs you: once an officer certifies in writing that you refused, the MVA suspends your license. [A48]
Why it matters: refusing the test does not avoid a suspension.
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A48
Trying to obtain a fake identification card, permit or driver's license can bring fines, prison or both under federal and state law. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A48
Lying about your age to buy, possess or get alcohol is illegal and, on top of other penalties, can lead to suspension of your license. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A48
For motor vehicle law violations the MVA may suspend, revoke, refuse or cancel a license, and it mails a notice giving the planned action, the reason and the steps to change or stop it. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A48
In most cases you may ask for an administrative hearing to explain why the action should not happen. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A48
If your license is suspended, revoked, refused or canceled you must surrender it to the MVA, and the suspension or revocation period starts when the MVA receives it. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A48
A suspension takes away your driving privilege for a time, and in some cases the MVA may grant a restricted license for set purposes such as work and school trips. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A48
Revocation is more serious than suspension: you may not drive until the MVA decides you can drive safely again. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A48
After a revocation you must wait a minimum period before asking the MVA to reinstate your license, and the MVA may say no. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A48
Cancellation is the most serious action: your driving privilege is ended and not restored. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A48
The MVA may cancel a license that should never have been issued, or one obtained with missing or wrong application information or by fraud. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A48
For a driver younger than 18, a parent or legal guardian may ask the MVA to cancel the license. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0048]

Glossary: restriction — a limit placed on your driving privileges [A47]. Implied consent — the agreement to testing that comes with driving in Maryland [A47]. Suspension — temporary loss of the privilege to drive [A48]. Revocation — loss of the license until the MVA decides you may drive again [A48]. Cancellation — permanent end of the driving privilege [A48].
Memory aid: suspend, revoke, cancel — each step is harder to undo than the one before [A48].
Misconception: hands-free calling is not allowed for a permit or provisional driver; only an emergency call is [A47].
